dataset: Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer; 569 observations, 30 numeric features
split: Stratified 80:20 train/test; training 70:30 fit/adaptation; adaptation split 50:50 monitoring/update. Monitoring is used for selection only; update subset for fitting; test is held out.
design: Severity sweep for mean shifts (0.25, 0.5, 1.0 SD), Gaussian measurement noise (0.25, 0.5, 1.0 SD), MCAR missingness (10%, 20%, 40%), no-shift control, and balanced outcome resampling. Three threshold profiles test selector sensitivity.
bootstrap: 2,000 paired bootstrap resamples of 10 seed-level differences; these intervals reflect repeated-split variability, not population-level uncertainty.
limitations: Within-dataset random-split robustness only; no independent external dataset or temporal cohort was available.
The adaptive selector uses labelled monitoring outcomes and an unshifted paired reference; it is not a deployable unsupervised drift detector.
Synthetic perturbations do not represent all real clinical shifts.
Balanced prevalence is created by resampling, not a prospective prior-probability shift.
Only two model families and ten seeds are used.
The test sample is small; calibration slope/intercept can be unstable.
Repeated splits overlap in observations; bootstrap intervals are not external-validation confidence intervals.
No clinical utility or patient-outcome claim is supported.
